ops.expect: Spire Gully right (Alpenkuhl), part of the Hairpin Crags, is reached from the same large pullout at the hairpin turns on SR-20 near Washington Pass used for Kangaroo Temple. Looking up toward South Early Winter Spire from the pullout, Spire Gully is the obvious gully just below and left; Alpenkuhl is its sunnier, south-facing right side (the left side is known as Tiger Wall). The approach is one of the shortest at Washington Pass — a direct walk/scramble of roughly 10-15 minutes straight up from the highway, snow-covered in early season and a worn boot path later in summer.
ops.value: Park at the apex of the hairpin turn on SR-20 below Washington Pass. Follow the climbers' trail up toward Quicksilver Slab and Spire Gully, then cut right into a dry creek bed and climb the slabs above it into the Ice Box. The upper, entrance slab has a fixed line; the lower slab does not. Both are smooth and slippery, and worse when wet.

results.summary: Keep this page as the climb of Mount Mathias from the Hoh River Trail (Glacier Meadows, the Blue Glacier and Glacier Pass) and rewrite the day plan, timing and text that described a Sol Duc to Hoh Bailey Range traverse.
results.evidence: The published route for Mathias (paired with Mount Mercury) is a Hoh River round trip: the steep snow finger between Mathias and Glacier Pass or the gullies to the Mercury-Mathias col, then Class 4 on the ridge, descending to Glacier Meadows; Mathias is described as a seldom-climbed peak, and the easiest line is Class 4. Detailed Bailey Range traverse reports cross the Hoh Glacier to Glacier Pass and exit by the Blue Glacier but do not climb Mathias. The row's approach, pitch_detail, approach_variants, main camp (Glacier Meadows), trailhead pin, approach_logistics, descent_text and pro_tips already describe the Hoh line; itinerary, timing, the middle waypoints, crowds, partner requirements, seasonal guidance, rope_note and one hazard described the traverse. The new day plan carries no mileages, hours, gains or pack weights rather than computed ones. (The Mathias & Mercury route page blocked direct fetch; its content was read from search extracts.)

expect.cal: Requires an Olympic NP wilderness permit in the quota-controlled Sol Duc/Bailey Range corridor; the route is really only in condition July–September, and doing it while the Bailey Range snowfields and Mathias's snow finger still hold snow (rather than bare ice/scree) makes for much faster, safer travel.

days.note: Start at the Sol Duc trailhead, climb through Deer Lake to High Divide, then continue the ridgeline past Cat Basin to a high camp near Eleven Bull Basin. Packs are heaviest here — full glacier kit plus five days of food.

days.note: Sidehill, mostly off-trail travel across the Baileys' famous narrow "catwalk" ridge sections below Mt Carrie and Stephen Peak, dropping into Ferry Basin to camp. Slow-going scree and heather traverses keep mileage low.

expect.totalNote: A serious point-to-point traverse from Sol Duc to the Hoh, roughly 55 miles and ~11,000 ft of gain over 5 days, tagging Mathias's loose Class 4 summit near Glacier Pass along the way with a roped glacier crossing on summit day.

value.cal: Needs an Olympic National Park wilderness permit for the nights at Glacier Meadows. The route is in condition roughly July to September, and it goes faster and more safely while the snow finger still holds snow rather than bare ice or scree.

days.title: Hoh trailhead to Glacier Meadows
days.objective: Reach the Glacier Meadows base camp
days.note: The long, mostly gentle Hoh River Trail through the rainforest, climbing steadily only in the last few miles out of the valley. A washed-out section near the top is crossed on a fixed ladder. Packs carry full glacier kit.

days.title: Blue Glacier, Glacier Pass and the Mathias summit
days.objective: Climb Mount Mathias by the snow finger or the Mercury-Mathias col and return to camp
days.note: Take the way trail to the Blue Glacier moraine, rope up and cross the glacier toward Snow Dome, then traverse the upper Hoh Glacier to Glacier Pass. Climb the steep snow finger between Mathias and the pass, or the gullies to the Mercury-Mathias col, to Class 4 rock on the summit ridge. Reverse the climb and recross the glaciers to Glacier Meadows. Mount Mercury is often added from the col.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Walk back down the Hoh River Trail to the trailhead
days.note: A long, mostly downhill trail day back to the Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center.

value.totalNote: An out-and-back from the Hoh: a long trail day in to Glacier Meadows, a roped glacier day to Glacier Pass and the summit ridge, and the walk out. Many parties add a spare day for weather or climb Mathias alongside Mount Olympus.
